display.title: The Secret of the Name of Hashem, Part 1
display.summary_short: How to pronounce Hashem's name properly, then the story of Rabbi Moshe Galanti of Damascus, who sets out to learn an Arab sheikh's secret of knowing whether a sick person will live.
display.summary_long: The storyteller begins by explaining how Hashem's name is written and read: the four-letter name was said aloud only by the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur, and today we read it as Ado-noi or Elokim depending on its vowels. He shows the common mistakes people make when saying it quickly and how to say it correctly. Then the story: long ago in Damascus lived Rabbi Moshe Galanti, a great Torah scholar who also mastered the seven worldly wisdoms. Only one man matched him, an Arab sheikh who could also tell, after praying in private, whether a sick person would recover. Troubled that the sheikh seemed to be shown the Book of Life, Rabbi Moshe arranges a meeting. The sheikh is so taken with his wisdom that he begs him to visit often. When the sheikh asks to learn the introduction to the seventh wisdom, Rabbi Moshe agrees to trade it only for the sheikh's secret. Reluctantly the sheikh tells him to fast for two days, immerse in a mikveh morning and evening, wear white and return on the third day. To be continued.
display.lesson: Hashem's name is holy, so we must say it carefully and correctly, especially in brachos and davening.
